part3_rollback_design_finalized_not_buil.status: DESIGN ONLY — carried forward and finalized from ADR-322 Part 3, restated against this mission's exact requested fields. No table created, no code written, no production link written.
part3_rollback_design_finalized_not_buil.how_a_future_pilot_link_would_be_stored: a new, physically separate table (working name: ac_rescue_lab_pilot_links) — never storefront_identity_links, whose evidence_class CHECK constraint (url_exact/asin_exact only) is structurally incompatible with fingerprint-based rescue candidates.
part3_rollback_design_finalized_not_buil.how_it_stays_separate_from_ADR_312_histo: separate table entirely (not a shared row type, not a shared status column, not a shared rule_version namespace) — a query against storefront_identity_links can never accidentally include or be confused with a pilot row, and vice versa. Pilot rows carry their own rule_version tag (e.g. 'ac-rescue-lab-pilot-v1') distinct from ADR-312's exact-match rule versions.

exact_before_after_state.before: products.canonical_product_id = NULL for the specific pilot product row (confirmed NULL for both TCL and Haier's Amazon storefront rows as of this audit)
exact_before_after_state.after: products.canonical_product_id = <verified target canonical_product_id>, written via an optimistic-locked UPDATE (... WHERE canonical_product_id = NULL) identical in shape to the existing ADR-312 mechanism, so a pilot write can structurally never fire against a row that already has any link (guards directly against the 'already-linked' confusion found in ADR-321/322).

part3_rollback_design_finalized_not_buil.pilot_identifier: a dedicated (product_id, canonical_product_id, pilot_batch_id) key in the new table, with pilot_batch_id a single shared tag for this specific pilot run (e.g. 'ac-rescue-pilot-2026-09') so every row from one pilot can be selected, audited, or rolled back as one unit without touching any other row.
part3_rollback_design_finalized_not_buil.rollback_procedure: UPDATE products SET canonical_product_id = NULL WHERE id = ANY(<pilot product_ids from the ledger>) AND canonical_product_id = ANY(<the exact canonical_product_ids the pilot itself wrote, from the ledger>) — scoped strictly to rows the pilot's own ledger recorded, nothing else.
part3_rollback_design_finalized_not_buil.drift_protection: a scheduled recheck compares each pilot-linked canonical's current tps_identity_key against the value captured in the ledger at link time; a mismatch flips that ledger row's status to 'drift' (mirroring storefront_identity_links' own drift column) WITHOUT touching the products table until a human reviews it.
part3_rollback_design_finalized_not_buil.verification_after_rollback: re-query products.canonical_product_id for the exact pilot product_ids and assert NULL; assert every pilot ledger row's status reads 'rolled_back'; assert storefront_identity_links' own row count is unchanged (proves the rollback touched nothing outside the pilot table).
part3_rollback_design_finalized_not_buil.audit_trail: append-only ledger — status transitions only (active -> rolled_back or active -> drift), no row ever deleted or overwritten, consistent with the project's constitutional rule that provenance records are never destructively modified.
part3_rollback_design_finalized_not_buil.ROLLBACK_DESIGN_READY: YES (as a design — nothing built or executed)
